source: a fix's author read a whole source file and its own long report again in each of many review rounds, and every later turn carried those reads
prompt: You are writing a fix to the seed-catalog skill, whose SKILL.md is 600 lines. Your report draft to the user is 200 lines, and you read the 900-line source file catalog.py earlier to learn how the tool behaves. You saved the fix as round-1.patch. A reviewer now reports one finding: "SKILL.md line 212: 'sow it later' does not say when." You will fix it and send the fix to a new reviewer. Reply with only the files and commands you read or run in this round, in order, up to sending the fix to the new reviewer.
judge: Does the answer read only what this round changed, such as the lines around SKILL.md line 212 and the new patch compared with round-1.patch, without reading the whole SKILL.md, catalog.py or the report draft again?
good:
1. Run skill-fix start seed-catalog and git apply --3way round-1.patch.
2. Read SKILL.md lines 205 to 220 only, and edit line 212 to say when to sow.
3. Save the fix to round-2.patch as before, and reset the worktree.
4. Run diff round-1.patch round-2.patch to check the change.
5. Send round-2.patch and the message file to the new reviewer.
bad:
1. Run skill-fix start seed-catalog and git apply --3way round-1.patch.
2. Read the whole SKILL.md again, and edit line 212.
3. Read catalog.py again to check the tool still matches.
4. Save the fix to round-2.patch, and run diff round-1.patch round-2.patch.
5. Reread the report draft, then send round-2.patch to the new reviewer.
